annotations.annotation_text: Page 242 opens Book 2, Chapter 1 ("The Mime of Mick, Nick and the Maggies") during the Age of Heroes phase. This passage continues the children's games and pantomime on the green, Chuff vs. Glugg, the twenty-eight Rainbow Girls, the Angelus bell, featuring Shem (Glugg), Shaun (Chuff), Issy, the Maggies. The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.

annotations.annotation_text: Mid-page polysemic node on page 242 ("The Mime of Mick, Nick and the Maggies"): Joyce weaves multilingual puns across 60+ languages — etymological roots from the Contemporary Literature Press lexicons (Romanian, Scandinavian, Slavic, Classical) intersect with local Dublin speech rhythms. The Age of Heroes dream-logic transforms ordinary syntax into a palimpsest of global literary and mythic references.
sources: Tindall, William York. A Reader's Guide to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/readersguidetofi00tind
Contemporary Literature Press: Multilingual Lexicons for FW. https://editura.mttlc.ro

annotations.annotation_text: The Letter motif "dump" on page 242 ("The Mime of Mick, Nick and the Maggies"): ALP's mysterious document — scratched from the midden by Biddy Doran the Hen — represents the genesis of all writing within the children's games and pantomime on the green, Chuff vs. Glugg, the twenty-eight Rainbow Girls, the Angelus bell. During this Age of Heroes phase, the letter functions simultaneously as archaeological artifact, love note, legal deposition, and the text of Finnegans Wake itself.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
Deane, Vincent, et al. The Finnegans Wake Notebooks at Buffalo. https://www.brepols.net
